# End to end high content bio-image analysis powered by AI

**OMERO-Screen** takes a 96-well immunofluorescence plate from an
[OMERO](https://www.openmicroscopy.org/omero/) server to a publication figure:
segmentation, feature extraction, cell-cycle assignment, storage,
classification and plotting as one reproducible workflow. It is built for cell
biologists running high-content screens, not for image-analysis specialists.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
**Active development.** OMERO-Screen is being developed alongside ongoing
research, so expect frequent changes and occasional breaking ones. A stable
release is planned for later in 2026. Pin a commit if you need an analysis to
stay reproducible.
:::

## What makes it different

### Rapid generation and adaptation of new models

Deep learning models for segmentation, tracking and classification have
revolutionised bioimage analysis, but remain difficult for experimentalists to
access. OMERO-Screen builds on [Cellpose](https://www.cellpose.org/) and
[Trackastra](https://github.com/weigertlab/trackastra), and adds a rapid
generation-and-deployment loop for classifiers. Its modular architecture means
models are selected from the command line (`--model`, `--track <model>`), so an
improved model can be swapped into the pipeline without touching the analysis
code.

### 4i / cyclic IF and automated tracking, without the coding

More advanced image analysis usually demands coding skills that most cell
biology labs do not have. OMERO-Screen integrates automated registration and
tracking pipelines, generating highly multiplexed single-cell data from a few
simple commands.

### Agentic AI integration

Because OMERO-Screen is driven entirely by terminal commands, it is directly
accessible to AI agents. We ship agent skills that run the whole pipeline —
from plate analysis through quantification to figure production — from natural
language prompts.

### Data integration and management

High-content IF data tends to grow exponentially and end up in chaos: thousands
of images, analysis spread across multiple tools and scattered files, and a
final figure that nobody can reproduce exactly. OMERO-Screen keeps raw data,
masks and analysis files together on an OMERO server. Screen images and
segmentation masks are viewed through local Zarr stores and napari plugins, and
single-cell data are queried from a local DuckDB database. This keeps terabytes
of high-content image analysis data in one well-organised, queryable form, and
keeps published results reproducible.
